questions.question: Name the movement that started at Naxalbari in Darjeeling district in West Bengal in 1967.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Naxalite Movement.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Naxalite Movement was a violent Maoist insurgency that emerged in India in 1967.
 
• It started in Naxalbari village in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, where peasants rose up against landlords and the government.
 
• The movement aimed to overthrow the Indian state and establish a communist society through armed struggle.
 
• The movement spread to other parts of India, particularly in rural areas where poverty, inequality, and social injustice were rampant.
 
• The movement has been responsible for numerous acts of violence and human rights abuses and has been designated as a terrorist organization by the Indian government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Bhoodan Movement,** also known as the Land Gift Movement, was a non-violent movement led by Vinoba Bhave in the 1950s and 60s, which aimed to persuade wealthy landowners to voluntarily donate land to landless peasants.
 
• ** The Chipko movement **was a non-violent environmental movement in the 1970s, which originated in the state of Uttarakhand, and involved women hugging trees to prevent them from being cut down.
 
• ** The Quit India Movement** was a mass civil disobedience movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1942, which aimed to force the British colonial government to grant India independence.

questions.question: During which season do North-east trade winds dominate India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Winter.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** North-east trade winds are the winds that blow from the north-east direction towards the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• ** These winds dominate India during the winter season, from November to February.**
 
• They bring dry and cool air from the Himalayas towards the Indian plains, resulting in clear skies and low humidity.
 
• The North-east trade winds are also known as the winter monsoon winds, as they are responsible for the winter monsoon season in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****Autumn:** During the autumn season, the monsoon winds start to withdraw from India, resulting in a transitional phase between the monsoon and winter seasons. The winds during this season are not dominated by the North-east trade winds.
 
• **Monsoon: **The monsoon season in India is dominated by the Southwest monsoon winds, which blow from the Arabian Sea towards the Indian subcontinent. These winds bring heavy rainfall to India and last from June to September.
 
• **Summer: **The summer season in India is dominated by the Southwest monsoon winds, which bring rainfall to most parts of the country. The North-east trade winds do not dominate India during this season.

questions.question: A situation in which the government may spend an amount equal to the revenue it collects is :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** a balanced budget.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A balanced budget is a situation where the government's spending equals the revenue it collects, resulting in no deficit or surplus.
 
• It means that the government is not borrowing money to fund its expenses, and it is not saving any excess revenue for future use.
 
• A balanced budget is considered fiscally responsible and sustainable as it helps to maintain economic stability and avoid inflationary pressures.
 
• However, achieving a balanced budget can be challenging, especially during times of economic downturn or when the government needs to invest in long-term infrastructure projects.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Deficit budget: It is a situation where the government's spending exceeds the revenue it collects, resulting in a budget deficit. To cover the deficit, the government may borrow money by issuing bonds or increasing taxes in the future.
 
• Surplus budget: It is a situation where the government's revenue exceeds its spending, resulting in a budget surplus. The surplus can be used to pay off the government's debt or saved for future use.
 
• Capital budget: It is a budget that focuses on long-term investments in infrastructure, such as building roads, bridges, and schools. Capital budgets are usually separate from the government's operating budget, which covers day-to-day expenses.

questions.question: The central theme of which of the following classical dance forms are the love stories of Krishna and Radha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Manipuri__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Manipuri
 
 
• Manipuri dance is the main classical dance form of India.
 
• The Manipuri language is named after its native place Manipur.
 
• The dance is based on Hindu Vaishnava themes and culminates with the love story of Radha and Krishna.
 
• The dance form is slow-moving and graceful, with the arms flowing to the fingers in a symbolic splendor.
 
• This dance form is based on its early customs and magical dance forms.
 
• Themes from the works of Vishnu Purana, Bhagavata Purana, and Gita Govinda are mainly used in this.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Chhau

 
 
• Chhau is a folk dance practiced in the states of West Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand.
 
• There are three types – Seraikela Chhau, Mayurbhanj Chhau and Purulia Chhau.
 
• This dance is a mixture of Samprik custom and dance and it depicts fighting techniques and animal movements and movements.
 
• This dance is performed by male dancers who are traditional artists or people of the local community.
 
 
 
• Sattriya
 
 
• Sattriya dance is a classical dance form of Assam.
 
• The founder of this dance is the great saint Srimanta Sankardev.
 
• This dance form is a tradition going on for more than 500 years.
 
• This dance is a tradition of the Vaishnava monasteries of Assam, known as Satra.
 
 
 
• Kuchipudi
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a famous dance form in Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• It is famous all over South India.
 
• The dance derives its name from the village Kuchipudi in Divi taluk of Krishna district, where Brahmins reside in this traditional dance practice.
 
• According to tradition, the Kuchipudi dance was originally performed only by men and that too only by men from the Brahmin community.

questions.question: Who among the following Mauryan emperors was known by the name of Piyadassi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Ashoka__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mauryan Emperor Ashoka __is the person whose name was also 'Devanampiya Piyadassi'.

 __
 
• "Devanampiya" means "Beloved of the Gods". It is often used by Ashoka in conjunction with the title Priyadasi, which means "He who regards others with kindness".
 
 
 
• Ashoka was the last major emperor of the Mauryan dynasty of India.
 
 
• He ruled the Mauryan dynasty from 268 BC to 232 BC.
 
• Following his successful conquest of the Kalinga country on the east coast, Ashoka renounced armed conquest.
 
• He adopted a policy that he called “conquest by dharma” (i.e., by principles of right life).
 
• His nature was full of sincerity. Ashoka conquered the Kalinga country (modern Orissa state) in the eighth year of his reign. It was at this time that he came in touch with Buddhism and adopted it.
 
• He built a number of stupas and monasteries and erected pillars on which he ordered inscribed his understanding of religious doctrines.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Bimbisara
 
 
 
• He was a king of the Magadha Kingdom who is credited with establishing imperial dominance in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He was the son of a minor king called Bhattiya, he belonged to the Haryana Dynasty, which is said to be the second imperial dynasty of Magadha.
 
• He ruled at a time when Gautama Buddha and Mahavira Vardhamana, the respective founders of Buddhism and Jainism, both started their teachings.
 
 
 
 

 Chandragupta Maurya
 
 
 
• He was the founder of the Maurya Empire.
 
• He was taught and counseled by Chanakya (also known as Kautilya).
 
• He defeated Seleucus I Nicator, one of the successful satrapies of Alexander the Great.
 
 
 
 

 Brihaddrata
 
 
 
• Brihadratha Maurya was the last ruler of the Maurya Empire.
 
• He was killed by his general, Pushyamitra Shunga, who went on to establish the Shunga Empire.
 
• According to the Puranas, Brihadratha succeeded Satadhanvan Maurya and ruled for seven years.

• It has been approved for a time period of four years, starting from 2021-22

__

questions.question: The main focus of the First Five Year Plan was to develop the _________ sector like agriculture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __agricultural sector.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• The First Five Year Plan in India was active between 1951 and 1956.
 
• The plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model.
 
• This plan gave priority to the agricultural sector__ of the country.
 
• The First Five Year Plan was presented before the parliament by Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• Gulzarilal Nanda was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission of India.
 
• Economist K N Raj is known as the architect of this plan.
 
• It was quasi-successful for the government.
 
• The target growth rate of the First Five Year Plan was 2.1% annual gross domestic product (GDP) growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] __Additional Information__

 
• The second Five Year Plan gave priority to the Industrial development of the country.

 
• The fifth Five Year Plan gave priority to agriculture, industry, and mines.

 
• The eighth Five Year Plan gave priority to the development of human resources(Human Model).

questions.question: How many Fundamental rights are provided by Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer __6 (Six)__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is considered the father of Fundamental rights in India.
 
• Fundamental rights are justifiable.
 
• In the original constitution, there were seven categories of fundamental rights in India.
 
• After the deletion of the Right to property by the 44th Amendment, it was reduced to six.
 
• The right to property is a legal right now.
 
• The Supreme court and the High Courts are considered as the guardians of Fundamental rights in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Now there are six categories of fundamental rights in India.

 
 
• Right to Equality.
 
• Right to Freedom.
 
• Right against Exploitation.
 
• Right to Freedom of Religion.
 
• Cultural and Educational Rights.
 
• Right to Constitutional Remedies.
